subject_line: Townsville and the making of Treading Air
email_body:
Dear Ariella,

I came to Treading Air, your 2016 debut with Affirm Press, through your profile as a Townsville writer now teaching at the University of New England, and noticed that your manuscript Hidden Objects was shortlisted for the 2012 Queensland Literary Awards.

I'd love to ask how the road from that manuscript to a published first novel shaped the book, and how teaching sits alongside your fiction.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is built from a few written questions you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger

subject_line: Peter Collie and the Amsterdam houseboat in The New Ships
email_body:
Dear Kate,

In The New Ships, Peter Collie, adrift after his wife's death, is pulled back to troubling events on an Amsterdam houseboat in the seventies, while the novel stays anchored in Wellington after the fall of the Twin Towers.

I'd love to ask why you set Peter's backward look against that particular moment, and how the book's moral choices took shape.

subject_line: Polluted rivers and Amazon pools in Where We Swim
email_body:
Dear Ingrid,

Where We Swim moves from solitary swims in polluted rivers in Aotearoa to pools in Arizona and the Peruvian Amazon, and I liked how it refuses one genre, part memoir, part travel, part nature writing. I also enjoyed your conversation about water and plot with Pip Adam on Elements.

I'd love to ask how you found a shape for a book built from so many separate swims.
